passages.text: So in the ninth year of Zedekiah’s reign, on the tenth day of the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon marched against Jerusalem with his entire army. They encamped outside the city and built a siege wall all around it.
passages.sermon:
Zedekiah was king in Jerusalem.
In the ninth year of his reign, something happened.
On the tenth day of the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar came.
Nebuchadnezzar was king of Babylon.
He brought his entire army with him.
They marched against Jerusalem.
They set up camp outside the city.
They built a siege wall all around Jerusalem.
passages.original: וַיְהִי֩ בִשְׁנַ֨ת הַתְּשִׁיעִ֜ית לְמָלְכ֗וֹ בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָעֲשִׂירִי֮ בֶּעָשׂ֣וֹר לַחֹדֶשׁ֒ בָּ֠א נְבֻכַדְנֶאצַּ֨ר מֶֽלֶךְ־ בָּבֶ֜ל ה֧וּא וְכָל־ חֵיל֛וֹ עַל־ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם וַיִּ֣חַן עָלֶ֑יהָ וַיִּבְנ֥וּ עָלֶ֖יהָ דָּיֵ֥ק סָבִֽיב׃

passages.text: And the city was kept under siege until King Zedekiah’s eleventh year.
passages.sermon:
Babylon’s army surrounded Jerusalem.
They kept the city under siege.
This siege lasted a long time.
The siege continued until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
passages.original: וַתָּבֹ֥א הָעִ֖יר בַּמָּצ֑וֹר עַ֚ד עַשְׁתֵּ֣י עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ צִדְקִיָּֽהוּ׃

passages.text: By the ninth day of the fourth month, the famine in the city was so severe that the people of the land had no food.
passages.sermon:
A famine struck the city.
This happened by the ninth day of the fourth month.
The famine became very severe.
The people of the land had no food.
passages.original: בְּתִשְׁעָ֣ה לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ וַיֶּחֱזַ֥ק הָרָעָ֖ב בָּעִ֑יר וְלֹא־ הָ֥יָה לֶ֖חֶם לְעַ֥ם הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: Then the city was breached; and though the Chaldeans had surrounded the city, all the men of war fled by night by way of the gate between the two walls near the king’s garden. They headed toward the Arabah, but the army of the Chaldeans pursued the king and overtook him in the plains of Jericho, and all his army was separated from him.
passages.sermon:
The city was breached.
The Chaldeans had surrounded the city.
All the men of war fled at night.
They escaped through the gate between the two walls.
This gate was near the king’s garden.
The men of war went toward the Arabah.
The army of the Chaldeans pursued the king.
They overtook the king in the plains of Jericho.
All the king’s army was separated from him.
passages.original: וַתִּבָּקַ֣ע הָעִ֗יר וְכָל־ אַנְשֵׁ֨י הַמִּלְחָמָ֤ה׀ הַלַּ֙יְלָה֙ דֶּ֜רֶךְ שַׁ֣עַר׀ בֵּ֣ין הַחֹמֹתַ֗יִם אֲשֶׁר֙ עַל־ גַּ֣ן הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְכַשְׂדִּ֥ים עַל־ הָעִ֖יר סָבִ֑יב וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ דֶּ֥רֶךְ הָעֲרָבָֽה׃ וַיִּרְדְּפ֤וּ חֵיל־ כַּשְׂדִּים֙ אַחַ֣ר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַיַּשִּׂ֥גוּ אֹת֖וֹ בְּעַרְב֣וֹת יְרֵח֑וֹ וְכָל־ חֵיל֔וֹ נָפֹ֖צוּ מֵעָלָֽיו׃

passages.text: The Chaldeans seized the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah, where they pronounced judgment on him.
passages.sermon:
The Chaldeans were the enemies of Jerusalem.
They seized the king of Judah.
They took the king to Riblah.
Riblah was where the king of Babylon stayed.
They brought the king of Judah before the king of Babylon.
They pronounced judgment on the king of Judah.
passages.original: וַֽיִּתְפְּשׂוּ֙ אֶת־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַיַּעֲל֥וּ אֹת֛וֹ אֶל־ מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶ֖ל רִבְלָ֑תָה וַיְדַבְּר֥וּ אִתּ֖וֹ מִשְׁפָּֽט׃

passages.text: And they slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes. Then they put out his eyes, bound him with bronze shackles, and took him to Babylon.
passages.sermon:
The Chaldeans captured King Zedekiah.
They killed the sons of Zedekiah while Zedekiah watched.
They blinded Zedekiah.
They put bronze shackles on Zedekiah.
They took Zedekiah to Babylon.
passages.original: וְאֶת־ בְּנֵי֙ צִדְקִיָּ֔הוּ שָׁחֲט֖וּ לְעֵינָ֑יו וְאֶת־ עֵינֵ֤י צִדְקִיָּ֙הוּ֙ עִוֵּ֔ר וַיַּאַסְרֵ֙הוּ֙ בַֽנְחֻשְׁתַּ֔יִם וַיְבִאֵ֖הוּ בָּבֶֽל׃ס

passages.text: On the seventh day of the fifth month, in the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar’s reign over Babylon, Nebuzaradan captain of the guard, a servant of the king of Babylon, entered Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
Nebuchadnezzar was the king of Babylon.
He had reigned for nineteen years.
Nebuzaradan was the captain of the guard.
Nebuzaradan served the king of Babylon.
On the seventh day of the fifth month, Nebuzaradan entered Jerusalem.
passages.original: וּבַחֹ֤דֶשׁ הַֽחֲמִישִׁי֙ בְּשִׁבְעָ֣ה לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ הִ֗יא שְׁנַת֙ תְּשַֽׁע־ עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ נְבֻכַדְנֶאצַּ֣ר מֶֽלֶךְ־ בָּבֶ֑ל בָּ֞א נְבוּזַרְאֲדָ֧ן רַב־ טַבָּחִ֛ים עֶ֥בֶד מֶֽלֶךְ־ בָּבֶ֖ל יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

passages.text: He burned down the house of the LORD, the royal palace, and all the houses of Jerusalem—every significant building.
passages.sermon:
Nebuzaradan was the captain of the guard.
Nebuzaradan served the king of Babylon.
Nebuzaradan entered Jerusalem.
Nebuzaradan burned the house of the LORD.
Nebuzaradan burned the royal palace.
Nebuzaradan burned all the houses in Jerusalem.
Nebuzaradan burned every important building with fire.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׂרֹ֥ף אֶת־ בֵּית־ יְהוָ֖ה וְאֶת־ בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־ בָּתֵּ֧י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֛ם וְאֶת־ כָּל־ בֵּ֥ית גָּד֖וֹל שָׂרַ֥ף בָּאֵֽשׁ׃

passages.text: And the whole army of the Chaldeans under the captain of the guard broke down the walls around Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
The Chaldeans were a powerful army from Babylon.
Nebuzaradan was their captain of the guard.
The whole Chaldean army followed Nebuzaradan.
They broke down the walls around Jerusalem.
passages.original: וְאֶת־ חוֹמֹ֥ת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם סָבִ֑יב נָֽתְצוּ֙ כָּל־ חֵ֣יל כַּשְׂדִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר רַב־ טַבָּחִֽים׃

passages.text: Then Nebuzaradan captain of the guard carried into exile the people who remained in the city, along with the deserters who had defected to the king of Babylon and the rest of the population.
passages.sermon:
Nebuzaradan was the captain of the guard for the king of Babylon.
He took the people who still remained in the city.
He also took those who had deserted to the king of Babylon.
He took the rest of the people as well.
Nebuzaradan carried all these people into exile.
passages.original: וְאֵת֩ יֶ֨תֶר הָעָ֜ם הַנִּשְׁאָרִ֣ים בָּעִ֗יר וְאֶת־ הַנֹּֽפְלִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר נָפְלוּ֙ עַל־ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל וְאֵ֖ת יֶ֣תֶר הֶהָמ֑וֹן הֶגְלָ֕ה נְבוּזַרְאֲדָ֖ן רַב־ טַבָּחִֽים׃

passages.text: But the captain of the guard left behind some of the poorest of the land to tend the vineyards and fields.
passages.sermon:
The captain of the guard was Nebuzaradan.
He left behind some people in the land.
These people were the poorest in the land.
He let them stay to work.
They took care of the vineyards.
They also worked in the fields.
passages.original: וּמִדַּלַּ֣ת הָאָ֔רֶץ הִשְׁאִ֖יר רַב־ טַבָּחִ֑ים לְכֹֽרְמִ֖ים וּלְיֹגְבִֽים׃

passages.text: Moreover, the Chaldeans broke up the bronze pillars and stands and the bronze Sea in the house of the LORD, and they carried the bronze to Babylon.
passages.sermon:
The Chaldeans entered the house of the LORD.
They found the bronze pillars there.
They found the bronze stands there.
They found the bronze Sea there.
The Chaldeans broke the bronze pillars.
They broke the bronze stands.
They broke the bronze Sea.
They took all the bronze from these items.
They carried the bronze to Babylon.
passages.original: וְאֶת־ עַמּוּדֵ֨י הַנְּחֹ֜שֶׁת אֲשֶׁ֣ר בֵּית־ יְהוָ֗ה וְֽאֶת־ הַמְּכֹנ֞וֹת וְאֶת־ יָ֧ם הַנְּחֹ֛שֶׁת אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּבֵית־ יְהוָ֖ה שִׁבְּר֣וּ כַשְׂדִּ֑ים וַיִּשְׂא֥וּ אֶת־ נְחֻשְׁתָּ֖ם בָּבֶֽלָה׃

passages.text: They also took away the pots, shovels, wick trimmers, dishes, and all the articles of bronze used in the temple service.
passages.sermon:
The Chaldeans entered the house of the LORD.
They took away the pots.
They took away the shovels.
They took away the wick trimmers.
They took away the dishes.
They took all the articles made of bronze.
The priests had used these bronze articles in the temple service.
passages.original: וְאֶת־ הַסִּירֹ֨ת וְאֶת־ הַיָּעִ֜ים וְאֶת־ הַֽמְזַמְּר֣וֹת וְאֶת־ הַכַּפּ֗וֹת וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־ כְּלֵ֧י הַנְּחֹ֛שֶׁת אֲשֶׁ֥ר יְשָֽׁרְתוּ־ בָ֖ם לָקָֽחוּ׃

passages.text: The captain of the guard also took away the censers and sprinkling bowls—anything made of pure gold or fine silver.
passages.sermon:
The captain of the guard took the censers.
He took the sprinkling bowls.
He took every item made of pure gold.
He took every item made of fine silver.
passages.original: וְאֶת־ הַמַּחְתּוֹת֙ וְאֶת־ הַמִּזְרָק֗וֹת אֲשֶׁ֤ר זָהָב֙ זָהָ֔ב וַאֲשֶׁר־ כֶּ֖סֶף כָּ֑סֶף לָקַ֖ח רַב־ טַבָּחִֽים׃

passages.text: As for the two pillars, the Sea, and the movable stands that Solomon had made for the house of the LORD, the weight of the bronze from all these articles was beyond measure.
passages.sermon:
Solomon made two pillars for the house of the LORD.
He also made the Sea for the house of the LORD.
He made movable stands for the house of the LORD.
All these items were made of bronze.
No one could measure the weight of the bronze in these articles.
passages.original: הָעַמּוּדִ֣ים׀ שְׁנַ֗יִם הַיָּ֤ם הָֽאֶחָד֙ וְהַמְּכֹנ֔וֹת אֲשֶׁר־ עָשָׂ֥ה שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה לְבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה לֹא־ הָיָ֣ה מִשְׁקָ֔ל לִנְחֹ֖שֶׁת כָּל־ הַכֵּלִ֥ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃

passages.text: Each pillar was eighteen cubits tall. The bronze capital atop one pillar was three cubits high, with a network of bronze pomegranates all around. The second pillar, with its network, was similar.
passages.sermon:
Solomon made two large pillars for the house of the LORD.
Each pillar stood eighteen cubits tall.
A bronze capital sat on top of each pillar.
The capital was three cubits high.
A network of bronze surrounded the capital.
Bronze pomegranates decorated the network all around.
The second pillar was the same as the first.
It also had a network and bronze pomegranates.
passages.original: שְׁמֹנֶה֩ עֶשְׂרֵ֨ה אַמָּ֜ה קוֹמַ֣ת׀ הָעַמּ֣וּד הָאֶחָ֗ד וְכֹתֶ֨רֶת עָלָ֥יו׀ נְחֹשֶׁת֮ וְקוֹמַ֣ת הַכֹּתֶרֶת֮ שָׁלֹ֣שׁ אַמָּה וּשְׂבָכָ֨ה וְרִמֹּנִ֧ים עַֽל־ הַכֹּתֶ֛רֶת סָבִ֖יב הַכֹּ֣ל נְחֹ֑שֶׁת וְכָאֵ֛לֶּה לַֽעַמּ֥וּד הַשֵּׁנִ֖י עַל־ הַשְּׂבָכָֽה׃

passages.text: The captain of the guard also took away Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the priest of second rank, and the three doorkeepers.
passages.sermon:
The captain of the guard acted.
He took Seraiah.
Seraiah was the chief priest.
He took Zephaniah.
Zephaniah was the priest of second rank.
He took the three doorkeepers.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּ֣ח רַב־ טַבָּחִ֗ים אֶת־ שְׂרָיָה֙ כֹּהֵ֣ן הָרֹ֔אשׁ וְאֶת־ צְפַנְיָ֖הוּ כֹּהֵ֣ן מִשְׁנֶ֑ה וְאֶת־ שְׁלֹ֖שֶׁת שֹׁמְרֵ֥י הַסַּֽף׃

passages.text: Of those still in the city, he took a court official who had been appointed over the men of war, as well as five royal advisors. He also took the scribe of the captain of the army, who had enlisted the people of the land, and sixty men who were found in the city.
passages.sermon:
Nebuzaradan was the captain of the guard.
He took people from the city of Jerusalem.
He took one court official.
This official was in charge of the men of war.
He took five men who served as royal advisors.
He took the scribe of the army commander.
This scribe had enlisted the people of the land.
He took sixty men from the people of the land.
These sixty men were found in the city.
passages.original: וּמִן־ הָעִ֡יר לָקַח֩ סָרִ֨יס אֶחָ֜ד אֲ‍ֽשֶׁר־ ה֥וּא פָקִ֣יד׀ עַל־ אַנְשֵׁ֣י הַמִּלְחָמָ֗ה וַחֲמִשָּׁ֨ה אֲנָשִׁ֜ים מֵרֹאֵ֤י פְנֵֽי־ הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִמְצְא֣וּ בָעִ֔יר וְאֵ֗ת הַסֹּפֵר֙ שַׂ֣ר הַצָּבָ֔א הַמַּצְבִּ֖א אֶת־ עַ֣ם הָאָ֑רֶץ וְשִׁשִּׁ֥ים אִישׁ֙ מֵעַ֣ם הָאָ֔רֶץ הַֽנִּמְצְאִ֖ים בָּעִֽיר׃

passages.text: Nebuzaradan captain of the guard took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
passages.sermon:
Nebuzaradan was the captain of the guard.
Nebuzaradan took these people.
He brought them to the king of Babylon.
The king of Babylon was at Riblah.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּ֣ח אֹתָ֔ם נְבוּזַרְאֲדָ֖ן רַב־ טַבָּחִ֑ים וַיֹּ֧לֶךְ אֹתָ֛ם עַל־ מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶ֖ל רִבְלָֽתָה׃

passages.text: There at Riblah in the land of Hamath, the king of Babylon struck them down and put them to death. So Judah was taken into exile, away from its own land.
passages.sermon:
The king of Babylon was in Riblah.
Riblah is in the land of Hamath.
The king of Babylon struck these men down.
He put them to death.
He did this at Riblah.
After this, Judah was taken into exile.
Judah was taken away from its own land.
passages.original: וַיַּ֣ךְ אֹתָם֩ מֶ֨לֶךְ בָּבֶ֧ל וַיְמִיתֵ֛ם בְּרִבְלָ֖ה בְּאֶ֣רֶץ חֲמָ֑ת וַיִּ֥גֶל יְהוּדָ֖ה מֵעַ֥ל אַדְמָתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, over the people he had left behind in the land of Judah.
passages.sermon:
Nebuchadnezzar was the king of Babylon.
He left some people in the land of Judah.
Nebuchadnezzar appointed a leader over these people.
He chose Gedaliah.
Gedaliah was the son of Ahikam.
Ahikam was the son of Shaphan.
passages.original: וְהָעָ֗ם הַנִּשְׁאָר֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ יְהוּדָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִשְׁאִ֔יר נְבֽוּכַדְנֶאצַּ֖ר מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֑ל וַיַּפְקֵ֣ד עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם אֶת־ גְּדַלְיָ֖הוּ בֶּן־ אֲחִיקָ֥ם בֶּן־ שָׁפָֽן׃פ

passages.text: When all the commanders of the armies and their men heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah as governor, they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah—Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan son of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, and Jaazaniah son of the Maacathite, as well as their men.
passages.sermon:
Nebuchadnezzar was the king of Babylon.
He appointed Gedaliah as governor over the people left in Judah.
Gedaliah was the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan.
All the commanders of the armies in Judah heard about this appointment.
Their men also heard about it.
The commanders and their men went to Gedaliah at Mizpah.
Ishmael was the son of Nethaniah.
Johanan was the son of Kareah.
Seraiah was the son of Tanhumeth, who was a Netophathite.
Jaazaniah was the son of the Maacathite.
These commanders and their men came to Gedaliah.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמְעוּ֩ כָל־ שָׂרֵ֨י הַחֲיָלִ֜ים הֵ֣מָּה וְהָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים כִּֽי־ הִפְקִ֤יד מֶֽלֶךְ־ בָּבֶל֙ אֶת־ גְּדַלְיָ֔הוּ וַיָּבֹ֥אוּ אֶל־ גְּדַלְיָ֖הוּ הַמִּצְפָּ֑ה וְיִשְׁמָעֵ֣אל בֶּן־ נְתַנְיָ֡ה וְיוֹחָנָ֣ן בֶּן־ קָ֠רֵחַ וּשְׂרָיָ֨ה בֶן־ תַּנְחֻ֜מֶת הַנְּטֹפָתִ֗י וְיַֽאֲזַנְיָ֙הוּ֙ בֶּן־ הַמַּ֣עֲכָתִ֔י הֵ֖מָּה וְאַנְשֵׁיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: And Gedaliah took an oath before them and their men, assuring them, “Do not be afraid of the servants of the Chaldeans. Live in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will be well with you.”
passages.sermon:
Gedaliah was the governor of the people left in Judah.
Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, appointed Gedaliah.
Gedaliah spoke to the commanders and their men.
Gedaliah took an oath before them.
Gedaliah said, “Do not be afraid of the servants of the Chaldeans.
Stay in the land.
Serve the king of Babylon.
It will go well with you.”
passages.original: וַיִּשָּׁבַ֨ע לָהֶ֤ם גְּדַלְיָ֙הוּ֙ וּלְאַנְשֵׁיהֶ֔ם וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֔ם אַל־ תִּֽירְא֖וּ מֵעַבְדֵ֣י הַכַּשְׂדִּ֑ים שְׁב֣וּ בָאָ֗רֶץ וְעִבְד֛וּ אֶת־ מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶ֖ל וְיִטַ֥ב לָכֶֽם׃ס

passages.text: In the seventh month, however, Ishmael son of Nethaniah, the son of Elishama, who was a member of the royal family, came with ten men and struck down and killed Gedaliah, along with the Judeans and Chaldeans who were with him at Mizpah.
passages.sermon:
Ishmael was the son of Nethaniah.
Nethaniah was the son of Elishama.
Ishmael belonged to the royal family.
In the seventh month, Ishmael came to Mizpah.
Ten men came with Ishmael.
Ishmael and his men attacked Gedaliah.
They killed Gedaliah.
They also killed the Judeans who were with Gedaliah at Mizpah.
They killed the Chaldeans who were with Gedaliah at Mizpah.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י׀ בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֗י בָּ֣א יִשְׁמָעֵ֣אל בֶּן־ נְ֠תַנְיָה בֶּן־ אֱלִ֨ישָׁמָ֜ע מִזֶּ֣רַע הַמְּלוּכָ֗ה וַעֲשָׂרָ֤ה אֲנָשִׁים֙ אִתּ֔וֹ וַיַּכּ֥וּ אֶת־ גְּדַלְיָ֖הוּ וַיָּמֹ֑ת וְאֶת־ הַיְּהוּדִים֙ וְאֶת־ הַכַּשְׂדִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁר־ הָי֥וּ אִתּ֖וֹ בַּמִּצְפָּֽה׃

passages.text: Then all the people small and great, together with the commanders of the army, arose and fled to Egypt for fear of the Chaldeans.
passages.sermon:
All the people were in Judah.
Some people were important.
Some people were not important.
The commanders of the army were also there.
All the people got up.
The commanders got up too.
They all left Judah.
They went to Egypt.
They were afraid of the Chaldeans.
They fled because they feared the Chaldeans.
passages.original: וַיָּקֻ֨מוּ כָל־ הָעָ֜ם מִקָּטֹ֤ן וְעַד־ גָּדוֹל֙ וְשָׂרֵ֣י הַחֲיָלִ֔ים וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ מִצְרָ֑יִם כִּ֥י יָרְא֖וּ מִפְּנֵ֥י כַשְׂדִּֽים׃פ

passages.text: On the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month of the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Judah’s King Jehoiachin, in the year Evil-merodach became king of Babylon, he released King Jehoiachin of Judah from prison.
passages.sermon:
King Jehoiachin ruled Judah.
Babylon took King Jehoiachin into exile.
He lived in exile for thirty-seven years.
Evil-merodach became king of Babylon.
This happened in the year Evil-merodach began to reign.
On the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month, Evil-merodach acted.
Evil-merodach released King Jehoiachin from prison.
King Jehoiachin left the prison house.
passages.original: וַיְהִי֩ בִשְׁלֹשִׁ֨ים וָשֶׁ֜בַע שָׁנָ֗ה לְגָלוּת֙ יְהוֹיָכִ֣ין מֶֽלֶךְ־ יְהוּדָ֔ה בִּשְׁנֵ֤ים עָשָׂר֙ חֹ֔דֶשׁ בְּעֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְשִׁבְעָ֖ה לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ נָשָׂ֡א אֱוִ֣יל מְרֹדַךְ֩ מֶ֨לֶךְ בָּבֶ֜ל בִּשְׁנַ֣ת מָלְכ֗וֹ אֶת־ רֹ֛אשׁ יְהוֹיָכִ֥ין מֶֽלֶךְ־ יְהוּדָ֖ה מִבֵּ֥ית כֶּֽלֶא׃

passages.text: And he spoke kindly to Jehoiachin and set his throne above the thrones of the other kings who were with him in Babylon.
passages.sermon:
Evil-merodach became king of Babylon.
He released Jehoiachin, king of Judah, from prison.
Evil-merodach spoke kindly to Jehoiachin.
He gave Jehoiachin a throne.
He placed Jehoiachin’s throne above the thrones of the other kings in Babylon.
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר אִתּ֖וֹ טֹב֑וֹת וַיִּתֵּן֙ אֶת־ כִּסְא֔וֹ מֵעַ֗ל כִּסֵּ֧א הַמְּלָכִ֛ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּ֖וֹ בְּבָבֶֽל׃

passages.text: So Jehoiachin changed out of his prison clothes, and he dined regularly at the king’s table for the rest of his life.
passages.sermon:
Jehoiachin was the king of Judah.
Babylon took Jehoiachin as a prisoner.
Evil-merodach became king of Babylon.
Evil-merodach released Jehoiachin from prison.
Jehoiachin changed out of his prison clothes.
Jehoiachin ate bread at the king’s table.
Jehoiachin ate at the king’s table for the rest of his life.
passages.original: וְשִׁנָּ֕א אֵ֖ת בִּגְדֵ֣י כִלְא֑וֹ וְאָכַ֨ל לֶ֧חֶם תָּמִ֛יד לְפָנָ֖יו כָּל־ יְמֵ֥י חַיָּֽיו׃

passages.text: And the king provided Jehoiachin a daily portion for the rest of his life.
passages.sermon:
Jehoiachin was a former king of Judah.
He lived in Babylon.
The king of Babylon showed him kindness.
The king gave Jehoiachin a daily portion of food.
The king provided this food every day.
Jehoiachin received this daily portion for the rest of his life.
passages.original: וַאֲרֻחָת֗וֹ אֲרֻחַ֨ת תָּמִ֧יד נִתְּנָה־ לּ֛וֹ מֵאֵ֥ת הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ דְּבַר־ י֣וֹם בְּיוֹמ֑וֹ כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י חַיָּֽו׃
